annotations.text:
spellcraft.io — three directions

Same content and structure in all three, so you're comparing feel rather than copy. Each row is one direction: Home, Docs, Plugins.

The docs page is the one to judge hardest — comprehensive docs are the priority, and it's where you'll spend the most time.

A · BLUEPRINT

Technical drafting. Paper ground with a fine grid, hairline rules, one drafting-blue accent, IBM Plex Sans + Mono. Monospace organises rather than decorates.

Strength: reads precise and unfussy; the lightest cognitive load of the three.
Tradeoff: the most conventional. Least likely to be remembered.

B · TERMINAL

Warm dark ground (not black), single amber accent, JetBrains Mono carrying the headings, dense tabular listings.

Strength: speaks the audience's native language instantly; the plugin table reads like tooling output.
Tradeoff: dark-only is a real constraint for long-form docs, and 'developer dark' is a crowded look.

C · FIELD MANUAL

Editorial. Literata for display, Source Sans for body, wide measure, diagrams as first-class content — note Figure 1 on the home page.

Strength: by far the best home for comprehensive docs; the chapter structure gives the docs somewhere to grow.
Tradeoff: the least 'developer tool' of the three — the serif could read as slow to a skimming engineer.
